Avery (sales): Hey team — Acme wants a short POC using a Dedicated endpoint. They asked how we want them to handle allowlisting and whether we can give them a single static egress IP for their firewall.
Jordan (solutions): We can support two common patterns: managed static egress (Redwood provides static EIPs) or customer-managed VPC peering / transit. Which does Acme prefer?
Tina - Acme IT: Prefer we don't peer for a POC. Ideally they give us an IP we can allowlist on our side. Can you provide an IP range or list?
Priya (neteng): For managed static egress we provide a small set of EIPs per region. For POCs we usually hand out up to 3 EIPs (for HA) and ask customers to allowlist those. We can also provide a temporary NATed hostname if they need fewer.
Sam (security): Two quick notes: 1) We need the POC service account scoped to least privilege and audit logs on. 2) If Acme's FW rules require mTLS we can support it but will need to enable client cert auth on the Dedicated endpoint.
Tina - Acme IT: mTLS not needed for now. We do require that the IPs are stable for at least the duration of the POC (2 weeks). Rotation ok with advance notice.
Jordan (solutions): That works. Flow we recommend for this POC:
- Redwood creates a Dedicated pool and Dedicated endpoint in us-west-2
- We allocate 3 managed EIPs and share them with Acme
- Create a scoped API key tied to the POC service account (expires in 14 days)
- Provide simple curl example and sample CIDR to allowlist

Priya (neteng): I'll provision the EIPs and the endpoint. Can you confirm which CIDR your firewall expects? Single IP entries or /32s?
Tina - Acme IT: We'll add /32s for each IP. Please send the exact addresses.
Avery (sales): On pricing — Acme asked if POC incurs Dedicated min commit. Short answer: we can run a short-term trial on Dedicated with usage-based billing for the POC duration (no long-term reserve) for deals under $X; otherwise we surface a short reserve quote. Will confirm numbers with finance.
Jordan (solutions): Example allowlist snippet for their firewall (replace with addresses we give):

```
allow ip from 203.0.113.45/32 to service.example.com port 443
allow ip from 203.0.113.46/32 to service.example.com port 443
allow ip from 203.0.113.47/32 to service.example.com port 443
```

Jordan (solutions): Sample curl for scoped POC key:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer POCTOKEN123" \\
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \\
  https://dedicated.us-west-2.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

Sam (security): Also ask Acme to sign the NDA + SOC2 excerpt requirement — we already have SOC2, but they usually ask for the report excerpt. I'll attach the standard intake doc in a sec.
DeployBot: Deploy of dedicated-endpoint/poce-1777 started by infra-ops at 1777777890 — status: provisioning.
Priya (neteng): Provisioning done (ETA ~5–10m). I'll post the EIPs when ready and add a note about rotation windows.
Tina - Acme IT: Thanks — please make sure the token only has the generate scope and cannot access our other infra.
Jordan (solutions): Will do. For the scoped token we'll set: scopes = ["generate"] and expiry = 14d. We will also attach audit logging and a single webhook for failure alerts if you want.
Tina - Acme IT: webhook optional for now. EIPs only, token, and expiry.
Priya (neteng): EIPs assigned: 198.51.100.12, 198.51.100.13, 198.51.100.14 (us-west-2). Please allowlist these /32s.
Avery (sales): I'll send the POC summary and next steps to the procurement/legal teams and confirm the billing arrangement.
Sam (security): Uploaded SOC2 excerpt to the shared folder and sent ACL checklist to Acme contact.
Tina - Acme IT: Confirmed allowlist updated. Testing now.
Jordan (solutions): Quick troubleshooting notes if connections fail: check that outbound DNS resolves dedicated.us-west-2.redwood.com to the EIP addresses, ensure strict egress rules allow 443 to those IPs, and verify the Authorization header contains the exact token.
Tina - Acme IT: Tests passing — we can hit the endpoint. Latency looks good.
Avery (sales): Great — action items: (1) Finance to confirm POC billing (Avery), (2) Jordan to deliver scoped token (done next), (3) Priya to log rotation window (48h notice).
Priya (neteng): Rotation window = 48h notice, will coordinate with ops.
Avery (sales): Thanks everyone — I'll loop in the AE and schedule a short demo next week. :thumbsup:
